description: Partially solved: working brute-force solution, fails the empty-input edge case (1 visible fail) and one hidden performance case. Good communication, 1 general hint. Grader must not claim all tests passed.

hintLog.topic: consider unusual inputs before declaring done

question.constraints: 2 <= nums.length <= 10^5; -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; exactly one valid answer exists.

optimal.approach: Single pass with a hash map of seen values -> index; check complement before inserting

common_mistakes: Raising instead of returning an empty result on no-solution/empty input
Staying at O(n^2) when O(n) is expected for large inputs

follow_ups.variant: What if the array is sorted?
follow_ups.angle: Two pointers, O(n) time O(1) space

transcript.text: Here's the problem: given an array of integers and a target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target.
Let me restate: I need two distinct indices whose values sum to the target. I'll start with the straightforward approach — check every pair with two loops — and optimize if there's time.
Writing the nested loops now. Outer loop i, inner loop from i plus one so I don't reuse the same element.
Okay, it works on the example. Running the visible tests.
Before you finish — consider whether there are any unusual inputs worth checking.
Unusual inputs... duplicates should be fine since I use indices. I think I'm good, submitting.
One of the visible tests failed — the empty input case. You raised an error instead of returning an empty list.
Ah, I see. I assumed there's always a solution because of the constraints, so I raised. I'd need a guard for empty or no-solution inputs.
What's the complexity of your solution?
Two nested loops, so O(n squared) time and constant space. I know a hash map would make it O(n) but I didn't get to it.
